picks.title: In An Era Of AI Slop, Meccha Chameleon Embraces Human-Crafted Chaos
picks.excerpt: Breakout hit Meccha Chameleon is being positioned as a deliberately human-crafted counterpoint to the wave of AI-generated 'slop' and copycats flooding storefronts. It is a craft-and-design argument about handmade chaos as a competitive differentiator against generative pipelines.
picks.rationale: Freshest pick and a concrete craft/design argument - handmade chaos framed as a deliberate differentiator against gen-AI pipelines.

picks.title: People Are Quickly Cloning Indie Games Using AI Tools
picks.excerpt: Solo developers are using AI coding tools to spin up playable clones of indie games within days, sometimes before the original even ships, and push them to storefronts first. It is a concrete workflow shift that is reshaping how small studios share and protect in-progress work.
picks.rationale: Actionable workflow shift for indie devs - AI clone-before-release changes how small studios reveal and protect in-progress work.

picks.title: Devs don't buy Steam disclosure claiming gen AI was a necessity: "I'm literally unemployed and I still make all of my assets by hand"
picks.excerpt: A dark-fantasy idle ARPG's Steam disclosure argued generative AI was a budget necessity, drawing sharp pushback from developers who say they still hand-make assets. The dispute is a live case study in how gen-AI reliance is being justified and contested inside real production pipelines.
picks.rationale: A live case study in how gen-AI reliance gets justified and contested inside real asset/production pipelines.
